answer: In cedar, B attestation branches are fixed and each wander is registered under every branch that vouches. A new wander needs a quorum q from separate branches; a branch's kth voucher burns k squared juniper, read and raised at commit, and batches are rejected. With B fixed, n clones cost about q cubed n cubed over three B squared juniper, so the marginal clone's bill rises steeply. It breaks if cedar can add branches, counters reset, or juniper is refundable.
